newsitem.title: CANADA: Hydro-Quebec signs US$1.8 billion of credit lines.
newsitem.headline: Hydro-Quebec signs US$1.8 billion of credit lines.

text.p: Hydro-Quebec said on Thursday it signed a deal on Wednesday with 44 banks worldwide to provide it with US$1.8 billion of standby credit lines.

The deal comprises three US$600 million agreements which were syndicated separately and simultaneously in Canada, the United States, Asia and Europe. The product was tailored to a seven-year term in Europe and a five-year term in North America.
The facilities will guarantee the Quebec government owned utility substantial savings on its credit facilities for several years, it said.

The agreements allow the utility to keep less cash on hand. They provide guaranteed access to funds from the credit lines, whatever the circumstances. This means funds would always be available if market conditions or unforseen destruction of company assets were to prevent the issue of commercial paper or other securities, the utility said.
Also, the absence of "force majeure" clauses in the agreements means that they are an important part of Hydro-Quebec's catastrophe insurance programs.

In Canada, Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce was lead manager, with co-leads National Bank of Canada and Toronto-Dominion Bank. In the United States and Asia, Royal Bank of Canada was lead manager, with syndication agent Chase Manhattan Bank, and documentation agent Societe Generale.
In Europe, Credit Suisse organized the transaction, with co-arrangers ABN-Amro and Caisse central Desjardins.
